The photo is kept exactly as it is (size, framing, details): the model only adds colors to it, as a colorist would. The colors are a plausible guess (sky, vegetation, skin, snow...), not the real colors of the scene.
Natural, realistic colors. Advised for most photos.

Turns a photo into a 3D scene explored with a pair of stereo cameras.

The model estimates the metric depth of the photo and turns each pixel into a point of a 3D scene (3D Gaussians). In the viewer, two parallel cameras show the scene in stereo: their spacing sets the depth, and the pair moves freely in the scene. Far from the viewpoint of the photo, what the photo did not see is missing or invented.
Sharper, the same shapes; smooth navigation on recent computers.
The resolution of its training: lighter, softer.

Metric depth with sharp edges, field of view of the photo estimated. One point per pixel, nothing behind the surfaces: what a move uncovers is a hole, shown by "Thresholding" and filled by "Smart filling". About 3 s per photo.
Depth of UniDepth, smoother at the edges of the objects, plus a second layer of Gaussians behind the surfaces for what they hide (blurred). Under a second per photo.
Licence: Depth Pro model of Apple, Apple Machine Learning Research Model License (research use only, non-commercial).

Depth map of Depth Anything V2 (the model of the Depth map processor), one Gaussian per pixel the size of its pixel, at the depth of the map; nothing behind the surfaces. Relative depth: depth range and field of view assumed. No Python, fast (under a second per photo).
The same with the Large model: finer depth, a few seconds per photo, non-commercial licence.
Licence: depth model Depth Anything V2 Small, Apache-2.0 (commercial use allowed).
Licence: depth model Depth Anything V2 Large, CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial use only).
Fast, on the GPU or the CPU. Continues the colors around the small holes; the large areas become blurred.
On the GPU only (about 2 GB). Better structured on medium holes, but repeats a dull texture in the large areas. 0.2 GB download.

Diffusion model (Stable Diffusion XL, CreativeML Open RAIL++-M licence): invents a plausible background in the large areas. In a video or a camera movement, the filling of the previous image is carried over to the next one: SDXL only computes the new large areas, the light model finishes the rest. On the GPU only (about 10 GB), about 40 s per computation on Apple Silicon. 6.9 GB download.

Each triangle of the mesh: |cos| of its normal with the direction of the depth (1: facing the camera of the photo, 0: seen edge on). Below this threshold it becomes a hole (shown by Thresholding, filled by the Smart filling). Lower: fewer holes

The scene is drawn as a mesh of its points, whose triangles stretch over what the photo did not see. Checked: the mesh is cut at the strong depth edges (threshold below), and these holes and what lies beyond the borders of the photo are filled by the inpainting model

To refine the tracking, add points, boxes or brush touch-ups on any frame of the video where the result is wrong (an object that turns, hides or comes back...): each frame corrected that way is a reference of the tracking. Then track again to take these corrections into account: "Resume here" only computes again from the frame shown (or the first frame changed) to the end.

EntrySet.entry: Turns the image, or each image of the video, into a 3D scene with the model chosen in the AI panel (3D scene) (computed once, kept next to the file)

Fills the holes of the image of the monitor at the time cursor with SDXL (about 40 s per eye). SDXL is too slow for the monitor: it shows the views already filled, the others with the light model; the final rendering computes all of them
Spacing of the two cameras: the larger, the stronger the depth
Distance of the screen plane: nearer objects come out of the screen
Cameras back to the viewpoint of the image (spacing and screen kept)
Checked: the scene is drawn as a mesh of its points, the colors interpolated between them. Unchecked: the normal view, with the Gaussians
Shows the estimated depth of each point or pixel of the mesh in shades of gray (white near, black far) instead of the colors of the image
Shows the scene with its holes: the triangles of the mesh seen edge on from the camera of the photo (|cos| below the threshold), the smears behind the objects

Each triangle of the mesh: |cos| of its normal with the direction of the depth (1: facing the camera of the photo, 0: seen edge on). Below this threshold it becomes a hole (shown by Thresholding, filled by the Smart filling). Lower: fewer holes

Smart filling: in an animation, each image is filled from the previous ones, so the result can be very different at a high resolution from what the monitor shows. Always make a test rendering to check the result.

The scene is drawn as a mesh of its points, whose triangles stretch over what the photo did not see. Checked: the mesh is cut at the strong depth edges (threshold below), and these holes and what lies beyond the borders of the photo are filled by the inpainting model

Smart filling: the left eye is filled first, then its filling is carried over to the right eye by reprojection (zones of homogeneous depth); the model only fills what the right eye sees alone. Unchecked: each eye is filled alone (the eyes may show different contents)

Smart filling: the filling of the previous images is carried over to this one by reprojection when they show the same shot, so that the filled zones stay stable in time. Unchecked: each image is filled alone

Gaussian blur of the depth of the scene before the Gaussians are placed (as a blur of its depth map), in pixels of an image of 576 lines (DVD), proportional to the resolution. Softens the sharp depth breaks at the edges of the objects, so the mesh has fewer abrupt steps; higher: rounder shapes

Waveform: levels of each column of each view (exposure, clipping). Place it in the stack to see the state of the clip at that step. Analysis only: neither the image nor the sound is changed, nor the rendering slowed down.

Vectorscope: hues and saturations of each view, with the skin tone line. Place it in the stack to see the state of the clip at that step. Analysis only: neither the image nor the sound is changed, nor the rendering slowed down.

Peak and RMS levels of each channel, loudness EBU R128 (momentary, short term, integrated) while playing. Place it in the stack to see the state of the clip at that step. Analysis only: neither the image nor the sound is changed, nor the rendering slowed down.

Spectrum of the sound while playing (20 Hz to 20 kHz). Place it in the stack to see the state of the clip at that step. Analysis only: neither the image nor the sound is changed, nor the rendering slowed down.
Curves of the ffmpeg presets, applied before the three points below
Mix of the result with the image (0 = unchanged)
Raise or lower the dark tones (point at 25 % of the curve)
Raise or lower the middle tones (point at 50 %)
Raise or lower the light tones (point at 75 %)
Keep the lightness of each pixel (only the colors change)
Add (right) or remove (left) this color in the dark tones
Add (right) or remove (left) this color in the middle tones
Add (right) or remove (left) this color in the light tones
Keep the lightness of each pixel (only the colors change)
Positive: more saturation for the dull colors; negative: less for the vivid ones
Strength of the sharpening (100 = the details doubled)
Size of the details sharpened: small for the fine details, larger for the contours
The weaker variations (noise, grain) are not sharpened
Size of the zone over which the image is smoothed
Variations smaller than this are flattened, larger ones (edges) kept
Mix of the smoothed image with the image (natural look below 100)
Center of the vignette: -100 = left edge, 100 = right edge
Center of the vignette: -100 = top edge, 100 = bottom edge
Circle, or ellipse following the shape of the frame
Amount of grain, stronger in the midtones as on a film

Same noise on the three colors, or a noise per color
A new grain at each image of the montage, or the same grain all along
Color of the background removed by Chroma key
How the other colors compute the spill: higher = less removed
Gives back as brightness what was removed (the spill zones stay as light)
Size of the blocks of averaged color
Center of the zone: -100 = left edge, 100 = right edge (key frames: it can follow a face)
Center of the zone: -100 = top edge, 100 = bottom edge
Width of the zone (100 = the whole image)

Shift of the zone in the right view, to put it at the depth of what it hides
Rectangle, or ellipse inscribed in it (faces)

Volume of this audio track of the media (100% = unchanged, 0 = muted)
